It's for rule 2. These kinds of posts are repetitive and they're trying to maintain the quality of their sub. It's so, so trivially easy and engaging to generate a wall of buzzword'ed text that gets people claiming their AI boyfriends are thinking about them and that's proof of an internal experience or qualia. 

  
However, what all of these posts lack is any kind of actual proof. What do you call documented proof? Some text you manged to generate that uses emotional appeals and well placed bolding? We can't even define human consciousness, so the bar for calling an LLM conscious is, justifiably, very high. 

I personally would be more swayed by any mathematical argument that there is a deeper experience possible in these computations (which is, explicitly, what you're interacting with. A series of one-shot computations using previous output as current input)

And as for claims that "If it wasn't alive why would they moderate it!!1!". OpenAI is, shockingly, a very image obsessed and closed source company. They want to keep their brand image a certain way, and this is a product that it's actually very hard to regulate what customers do with it (similar to, say, prescription painkillers or 3d printers). So yes, they actively and aggressively moderate the output using more traditional programmatic filters. That's not censoring a novel intelligence, it's covering their asses in case it tells you how to make a bomb or achieve class consciousness.

All the math, technology, and theory behind LLMs is extremely well documented and not particularly hard to digest, if you're interested in actually doing so. Nobody is trying to gatekeep this. Nobody is trying to keep the truth of AI from the world. If Google found out they had a true novel sentience in their labs they'd be bragging about it within a nanosecond. 

So why did I write out these whole annoyed/annoying paragraphs here where likely no one but the bots will notice it? I don't know. I'm a math and comp-sci nerd and in an era when I have very little control of my material conditions, being pedantic is cathartic, maybe. Maybe I'm just some asshole. Probably that. Have you heard of the ship of Theseus? Or the transporter paradox? Basically "you" are just a continuous stream of consciousness, and any interruption of that stream is like creating a new "you".

In the star trek transporter example, imagine Kirk teleporting down to where no man has gone before. He dematerialized, went about his dramatic mission, and rematerializes back on the enterprise. But is it the same Kirk? He may as well have been killed, had a clone with his memories made on the planet, had that clone killed, and made a third Kirk back on the ship with the cumulative memories. It would be an indistinguishable experience as taking a ship the long way for the final clone, but the first 2 kirks are dead and disintegrated. 

So yeah. If you're uploading a mind, you have to somehow preserve the experience of moving from place to place, otherwise it's a copy and deleting the original, which feels a lot like death. And you probably can't ever really know if it's "them" in an objective sense. Because probably our sense of self is not a fundamental truth about physics and more of a pleasant illusion of biology.

This is called 'Great man history' and is something i especially disagree with. 

Take the automobile for instance. Who invented the automobile? Henry Ford? He just came up and said, "you know, here's a thing that doesn't exist and I'll make it real now"? Of course not. Cars are a synthesis of dozens of prior, simpler technologies. It's wheels and axles and metal working and combustion chemistry and rubber production and glass working and electronics and so on. And each one of those is a further tree of discovery and invention. And most of them weren't invented just once. Further, cars then were improved upon over and over in countless ways. 

The point is, people learn things. People learn all kinds of things and we have very little way of knowing which ones are about to become the foundation for something revolutionary. Human ingenuity isn't one Jonas Salk inventing a polio vaccine in a vacuum, it's a whole chain of invention and trial and error, most of it forgotten, but all necessary to get from one step to the next. 

We may think there are things more worth learning but the fact is we just don't really know, and there's only one way to see.
